To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the C-terminus of AdE1As forms a series of alpha-helices that are anchored in CtBP by the PXDLS sequence through a beta-turn-->alpha-helix structural isomerisation.

the conformational rearrangements that occur upon CtBP1 binding of Ad12E(1A) are dependent on the sequence of the Ad12 E(1A) C-terminus, and that the C-terminal sequence of other adenovirus E1A proteins are also likely to be alpha-helical.
the C-terminal binding proteins (CtBPs) are a family of proteins that bind to a conserved PXD/LS motif found within a number of proteins including the adenovirus early region E1A.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural and biochemical characterisation of the interaction between Ad12E1As and CtBP1.
the structural basis of protein-protein interactions between the E1A proteins of the adenoviruses and CtBP.
the elucidation of the structure of a protein-protein interaction between a viral oncogene product (AdE1As) and a cellular protein (CtBP).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ad12E(247)-N (266) peptide forms a series a beta-turns in the absence of protein and that the CtBP1 binding site is formed by a beta-turn-->alpha-helix isomerisation.
Ad12E12A residues (255)-P-V(260), and possibly the region (254)VP-V(258), are important for the interaction with CtBP.
the C-terminal region (241)I-NDLCVK(261)-N-terminus of the Ad12 early region 2A protein adopts a beta-turns-alpha-helix conformation upon binding to the C-terminal-binding protein 1 (CTBP1).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CtBP1-Ad12E1A interaction is a two-step process, with the first being a recognition step and the second a conformational change in the Ad12EIA sequence.
the CtBP-binding region of Ad12 E1A is a flexible alpha-helix that is capable of forming beta-turns in the absence of protein.
AdE1As bind to CtBP1 through a PXDLS motif which is embedded in an alpha-helices and that CtBP1 binds to the N-terminal half of the AdE1A protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CtBP1 binds to the C-terminus of AdE1As and that this region of Ad12 E1A is alpha-hellical in the absence of the protein.
the CtBP binding motif is not necessarily a beta-turn but can be an alpha helix.
CtBP1 binds to the PXDSL motif through a conformational rearrangements of the C-terminal beta-turn to an helical conformation.
